sources.citation: Human Relations Area Files. SS16 Pemon file (microfiche; sources incl. Simpson, George Gaylord 1940 'Los indios Kamarakotos' and Armellada, Cesáreo de 1943-46, in English translation; processed 1966-69).
sources.note: Nothing on Bonari; lexical/classificatory mention only.

sources.citation: Meira, Sérgio. 2006. Cariban languages. In Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed. (family survey)
sources.note: Family-level remarks on rhythmic iambic stress (Tiriyó etc.) and other patterns; does not mention Bonari.
sources.venue: Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed. (family survey)

sources.citation: Gildea, Spike. 2003. Proposing a new branch for the Cariban language family. Amerindia 28: 7-32.
sources.note: Name appears only in reproduced and proposed classification tables; p. 10 adds the general remark that in early Cariban materials 'most sources have been unable to reliably indicate stress'. Nothing specific on Bonari prosody.

sources.citation: Weisshar, Emmerich. 1979. Die Stellung des Warao und Yanomama in Beziehung zu den indigenen Sprachen Südamerikas nördlich des Amazonas: Studien zur genetischen und areal-typologischen Klassifikation. Doctoral dissertation (archive.org copy in the theses-and-dissertations / leiden-university collection). [A mentioned this title in an angle outcome as 'Migliazza? 1979' but did not list or open it; author is Weisshar.]
sources.note: Nothing about Bonari prosody; the only 'Akzent' entries belong to an Island Carib (Dominica/British Honduras, Taylor) phoneme table and to generic lists of phonological features used for areal typology.

sources.citation: Loukotka, Čestmír. 1968. Classification of South American Indian languages. Los Angeles: UCLA Latin American Center.
sources.note: Lists Bonari with sample words and source; would confirm there is no further Bonari material beyond Souza 1875. Not expected to contain a stress statement.

sources.citation: Hübner, Georg & Theodor Koch-Grünberg. 1907. Die Yauapery. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 39: 225-248 (pp. 235-236: comparison of 10 Bonari words with Yauapery).
sources.note: Only a 10-word Yauapery/Bonari comparison (panari/panare, tuná/tuna, uató/uatú..) and the remark that Yauapery is closest to Bonari; no phonological statement.

sources.citation: Adam, Lucien. 1893. Matériaux pour servir à l'établissement d'une grammaire comparée des dialectes de la famille caribe. (Bibliothèque linguistique américaine, XVII.) Paris: J. Maisonneuve.
sources.note: No accent or stress discussion anywhere in the book (no occurrences of 'accent'/'tonique'); the phonetic chapter covers segment correspondences and syllable loss. Bonari forms (uque-ré, te-comi-nhua, uatu, weiu, u-puité-n, purená) are cited with Souza's acute accents retained -- wordlist marks only.

sources.citation: Brinton, Daniel G. 1892. Studies in South American Native Languages. Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 30(137): 45-105; sect. VI 'The Bonari dialect of the Carib stock', pp. 82-84.
sources.note: 39-item English-Bonari vocabulary; many items printed with a final accent mark (purena', urapa', panare', nurvba', iriopo', abeno', uquere', usiu', darara', tiada', iriane') reproducing Souza's final acutes -- an orthographic hint at final prominence in a wordlist, not a statement. The only commentary concerns Tupi loanwords (tupan, tamunha, urapa, tiada, tapaiuna).
sources.venue: Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society

sources.citation: Fonseca, João Severiano da. 1880. Viagem ao redor do Brasil, 1875-1878. Vol. 1. Rio de Janeiro: Typographia de Pinheiro & C.
sources.note: No phonological commentary on Bonari; the forms are listed among cognates (e.g. 'Tuna em galibi.. Nos bonaris é tunah, nos macusis duna'). General remarks on 'prosodia'/'syllaba' elsewhere in the volume concern Tupi and Guaycuru, not Bonari.

sources.citation: Souza, Francisco Bernardino de. 1875. Commissão do Madeira: Pará e Amazonas, pelo encarregado dos trabalhos ethnographicos. 2.ª parte. Rio de Janeiro: Typographia Nacional. Bonari wordlist pp. 77-78 (Google scan binds 1.ª parte 1874 + 2.ª parte 1875 together).
sources.note: Nothing. It is a bare ~60-item Portuguese-orthography wordlist ('palavras do dialecto Bonaris') obtained from the vicar of Silves from the last surviving speaker; no phonological commentary. Many items are written with a final acute accent (Cunobá, Iriané, Uqueré, Iriopó, Nurubá, Pianaré, Pademacá, Uruá, Tiadá, Urapá, Purêná, Meacabá, Timiará), an orthographic hint at final prominence only, not a statement.

sources.citation: Souza, Francisco Bernardino de. 1875. Commissão do Madeira: Pará e Amazonas.. 3.ª parte. Rio de Janeiro: Typographia Nacional.
sources.note: No Bonari material at all (a full-text search for stress/accent scanned text); checked only to locate the list.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page bona1255 and Wikipedia 'Bonari language'
sources.note: Nothing; confirm the language is extinct and attested only by Souza's 1875 wordlist, with Girard 1971 as the sole scholarly discussion.

sources.citation: Girard, Victor. 1971. Proto-Carib phonology. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley (pp. 116-117 on Bonari).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only scholarly treatment of the Bonari list; if anyone commented on the accent marks in Souza's transcription or on stress, it would be here. Likely only classificatory remarks.
